summary: L. Johannes Frohnmeyer (1850–1921) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Basel Mission from circa 1870 to 1875, later serving as its inspector of missions (1876–1905) and as a Fellow at the University of Madras.

L. P. N. Perera worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a supervisor at the Vidyodaya Campus of the University of Sri Lanka and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti (1902–1987) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, Sinology, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from Eötvös Loránd University and studied at Paris under scholars including Pelliot and Maspero, later serving as Professor of Central Asian Languages (1940–1974).

Lajos Lóczy (1849–1920) was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Zurich and ETH Zurich (1869–1874), joined the Hungarian National Museum in 1874, and became Professor of Geography at Eötvös Loránd University in 1889.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshman Sarup (1894–1946) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as University Professor of Sanskrit at Panjab University, attested in 1947.
Lakshmanacharya was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held a post at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala, Mathura, attested in 1889 and 1900, serving there as an अध्यापक.

Lakshmi Swaminathan (1914–2012) worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Queen Mary's College (circa 1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (circa 1932–1938), later serving as a Retired Lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) worked in Buddhist, religious, and Indological studies. After earning degrees from Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur, he held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Amherst, Haverford, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology. He held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested in 1939, and served as Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Vadodara.

Lama Jabb works in Tibetology. He has served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and, attested in 2026, as Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford.

Lama Jampa Thaye (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Manchester, studied under Karma Thinley Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa, and taught at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Isebaert (born 1955) works in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Albert Joris van Windekens (~1974–1981) and served as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain from circa 1984 to 2020.

Lambert Schmithausen (born 1939) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker, and served as associate professor of Indology at Münster (1970–1973) and on the Advisory Board at Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lan Wu is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. from Columbia University (2008–2016), she taught at the University of New Mexico (2015–2016) and Mount Holyoke College (2023).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University by 1986 and served as Professor (attested 1997) and Professor Emeritus (2021) at the University of San Diego.

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–1999) and Oxford (~2000–2015), and served as Pali Text Society President (2002–2003).
